All dog owners and lovers know that well-trained dogs develop into sociable and loving creatures which is almost certain to enhance the quality of life for you, your family, and the dog itself. So, training a dog has many benefits.

Disciplined dogs are unlikely to fight with other dogs. A dog trained to obey simple commands is a joy to own. Walking in the park with an obedient dog alongside you is one of life’s most pleasurable experiences.

Obedient dogs will be friendly to young children. Dogs should build up a good relationship with children wherever possible. Youngsters can be frightened by unruly behaviour, such as barking or growling and jumping up them can lead to phobias as they grow up.

Time spent training a puppy creates a loving bond between the dog and its master. This is an invaluable experience. It will lead to a special, lasting, friendship that benefits both you and your dog, ensuring a happy and contented life for man and his best friend. With proper home-made dog food, guidance, and discipline, your dog should live to a great age, so time invested in training is time well spent. It is a fun activity, bringing a sense of achievement and contentment to all who take part.

Here are a few basic commands your dog should learn:

Down: Teaching a dog to lay down. This is one of the main aspects of any training programme and a good command to begin with.

Heel: Teaching a dog to walk beside you, at the same pace, without pulling on the lead, is vital for enjoying a walk together. A collar, attached to a strong lead, is essential for dog training. Unfortunately, it may be necessary to restrain a dog so a good lead is vital. Leads are readily available from stores selling dog grooming supplies.

No: Your dog must understand the word ‘no’. It can save you trouble and avoid harmful and embarrassing situations in the future.

Sit: This is another basic training command and one that needs mastering from the outset to control a dog’s behaviour.

Stay: Another important command. When your dog responds to this, you will know where your dog is, and you can be confident of leaving him alone for a short while if needed.

Teaching your dog these basic commands will improve the relationship between you and your pet and increase the enjoyment you share. Ideally, it is preferable to start training your dog while still a puppy. Younger dogs are receptive to training commands, older dogs slower to learn. However, if puppy training is impossible, begin training at the earliest opportunity.

Training shows your dog that you are the boss. Your dog should understand from the outset as this will eliminate behavioural problems and means that a dog is a loved and valued member of the family.

Untrained dogs become depressed and despondent. They are unhappy and display symptoms of anxiety and confusion. Training will give your dog a purpose in life, and your dog will gain pleasure from pleasing you.
The Value of a Well Trained Dog
